topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture theme on cancer evolution, contextualises it within previous lectures, and outlines the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic Clonal Succession and Epigenetic Plasticity in Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumor progression is driven by the Darwinian selection of successive genetic mutations alongside non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Stem Cell Hierarchies in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how normal tissue hierarchies and stemness properties influence which cell types are susceptible to initiating and sustaining malignant growth.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Drivers of Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stroma create permissive conditions necessary for malignant outgrowth and maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental and Computational Methods for Profiling Tumors and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the modern sequencing, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic technologies used to map tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions in human tissues.

topics.label: Integrated Evolutionary Model of Cancer Progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates the multi-layered contributions of mutational burden, epigenetic state, cell of origin, and microenvironmental co-evolution into a unified evolutionary framework.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and indicates the topic for the following session.
